title: Extracts from the rules and minutes of the Free Christian Baptist General Conference of New Brunswick

creators.name: Free Christian Baptist General Conference of New Brunswick

summary: Extracts from the rules and minutes of the Free Christian Baptist General…. is an ecclesiastical record and denominational handbook compiled in the mid-19th century. It presents the governance framework and proceedings of the Free Christian Baptist General Conference of New Brunswick. The likely topic is church organization: how conferences and district meetings are structured, how decisions are made, and what actions were resolved to support and defend the denomination’s work. The book first outlines rules defining the composition and duties of the General Conference and District Meetings, including officers, quorums, mandatory attendance of ordained elders, recognition of Conference decisions by all churches, district boundaries, selection of messengers, and the limited but clear powers of districts (with major cases referable to the General Conference). It mandates aid to churches facing important trials, provides for receiving new congregations, assigns preachers to district meetings, requires districts to send lay messengers and records to the Conference, and stipulates unanimity for rule changes. The minutes then record a July gathering at Lincoln where a moderator and clerks were appointed, additional rules were adopted, and two major initiatives were approved: creating a voluntary General Conference Fund (with annual, publicly reported accounts) and preparing a published work to state the body’s origin, statistics, faith, constitution, discipline, and marriage form. Further actions include appointing treasurers, naming a messenger to a sister conference, setting the next General Conference, organizing six district jurisdictions with meeting times and attending elders, requiring public church reports before business sessions, and directing the publication of these extracts for distribution to all churches.
